text: A constitutional referendum took place in Niger on 24 September 1989, resulting in the adoption of a new constitution that established the country as a one-party state, with the National Movement for the Society of Development designated as the only legally permitted political party. The government structure would follow a presidential system, while the Armed Forces—having governed since the 1974 military coup—would retain significant influence. The referendum was approved by 99.3% of voters, with a turnout of 94.9%. The first elections under this new constitution occurred later that year on 12 December.
